findings.title: Order is committed before inventory allocation succeeds
findings.explanation: For an out-of-stock SKU, the new commit persists the inserted order before the conditional inventory UPDATE returns zero rows and raises ValueError. The exception handler's rollback cannot remove that already committed order, leaving an order for inventory that was never allocated. This is a direct regression in the changed transaction boundary.
findings.failurePath: apply_order begins a transaction, inserts the order, and commits at line 19. The inventory UPDATE then returns rowcount 0 for an unavailable SKU; the function raises, calls rollback, and re-raises, but the committed order remains.

candidates.invariant: Creating the order and decrementing inventory must be one atomic operation: failed inventory allocation must not persist the order, and successful allocation must persist both changes together.
candidates.counterexample: When inventory is unavailable, the INSERT is committed before UPDATE raises, so rollback cannot remove the order. When inventory is available, UPDATE occurs after the commit and may remain uncommitted, allowing the inventory decrement to be lost independently of the committed order.
candidates.evidenceNeeded: Confirm caller/test expectations for atomic order-plus-inventory behavior and the connection's transaction/commit ownership.
